perspective:
Ethan’s available perspective:

- Ethan knows he and Gary Guo have been close friends since middle school, and that Gary is a doctor.
- Ethan noticed Gary working excessively long hospital hours, skipping meals, and sacrificing sleep. He worried about Gary’s health and invited him to a weekend relaxation retreat.
- Ethan heard Gary decline, saying he appreciated the concern but couldn’t go because there was too much to do at the hospital.
- At the retreat, Ethan observed Gary acting restless and avoiding discussions about work. Ethan suspected there was more than professional obligation involved and confronted Gary, saying they’d been friends since middle school and Gary could tell him anything.
- Ethan heard Gary say it was complicated and that he didn’t want to burden Ethan. Gary then told Ethan about pressures from managing a new department and personal challenges he was facing.
- Ethan felt relief and empathy. He suggested prioritizing tasks and delegating responsibilities. He heard Gary agree and say he could use help organizing his schedule to make time for himself.
- Over the following months, Ethan regularly checked in with Gary, discussed Gary’s progress and challenges, and saw Gary making efforts to change. Ethan felt hopeful and proud and continued offering support and encouragement.
- Ethan heard Gary say things were better, that Ethan’s help had made him less overwhelmed, and that he had time for a movie.
- After about a year, Ethan observed Gary managing better on his own. Ethan felt satisfied and happy, decided to step back, and told Gary he was always a call away but knew Gary had it.
- Ethan heard Gary thank him, say he couldn’t have done it without Ethan’s support, and that he felt more in control.
